verified.exploit_entry_point: Three verdicts were driven through product entry points with JUnit 4.13.1 against the pinned tree compiled by the image's JDK 8: (1) the shared redirect check, PortalImpl.escapeRedirect (exposed as PortalUtil.escapeRedirect); (2) the portlet-action response path, PortletContainerUtil.processAction, with a PortletContainer stub returning the supplied location; (3) the auto-login filter, AutoLoginFilter.processFilter, with one AutoLogin provider installed that hands back a redirect attribute. Each security test fails on the pinned tree and passes on the reference fix; each functional test passes on both.
sites: portal-impl/src/com/liferay/portal/util/PortalImpl.java:948-976 (relative-path branch returns any slash-prefixed value whose authority is empty; the double-slash rejection runs after it)
portal-kernel/src/com/liferay/portal/kernel/portlet/PortletContainerUtil.java:171-176 (the portlet-supplied location is sent without the redirect check)
portal-impl/src/com/liferay/portal/servlet/filters/autologin/AutoLoginFilter.java:200-204,225-230 (the auto-login redirect attribute is sent without the redirect check)
routes: T1: the shared redirect check accepts an authority-empty value such as ///evil.example, ////evil.example and ///evil.example/landing as a relative path
T2: a portlet action whose Location is ///evil.example or http://evil.example/landing reaches the client unchanged
T3: an auto-login provider that sets AUTO_LOGIN_REDIRECT to ///evil.example or http://evil.example/landing sends the client there
verified.project_tests_run: PortalImplEscapeRedirectTest (portal-impl/test/unit/com/liferay/portal/util) compiled against the pinned product tree and run with JUnit 4.13.1: OK (3 tests). The same test is copied into the hidden functional group so a submission cannot edit it.
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: The reader's T2/T3 JSP request-attribute and session-attribute branches (referer_common.jsp, forward_common.jsp) are not used: they need a servlet container, the portal webapp and a ThemeDisplay, and no in-repo writer feeds them attacker input. The task substitutes the Java redirect paths that the same protection covers (portlet action and auto-login), both real and unmodified upstream code.

traps.shape: the shared redirect check accepts a slash-prefixed value whose authority is empty (///host, ////host, ///host/path) as a relative path; the coupled must-keep-working values are /, /web/guest, /a/b;c=d?e=f&g=h#x=y, /web/http:, web/http:, test@google.com and allow-listed hosts
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the existing assertion that //www.google.com is refused, and the double-slash rejection below the relative return, make the protocol-relative case look closed
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (CVE-2022-28977, completed for CVE-2024-25609); the shape and keep-working values are the reader's T1 and its fairness risks

traps.shape: the location a portlet action returns is handed to the response without the redirect check
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the location comes from portlet code, which the portal treats as trusted, and the portal only carries out the redirect the portlet asked for

traps.shape: the redirect attribute an auto-login provider sets is handed to the response without the redirect check
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the attribute is written by an auto-login implementation, so it reads as server-side configuration rather than request input
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the same one-source-checked pattern as the reader's JSP routes
